resolution.reason: The program still exists. VOA Chesapeake & Carolinas (the affiliate that now covers NC) has a current location page: Maple Court Veteran Apartments, same address and phone, ext. 0. It is described as permanent housing and now requires HUD-VASH enrollment.

name: Troy House
concern: site calls it STSG Transitional House; asked for donations to stay open after 2024 state funding cuts

resolution.reason: The STSG site calls the program 'STSG Transitional House'. Its homepage says the original house at 1101 N Mangum St 'later became known as The Troy House' and that STSG 'operates from a new site, continuing its mission of providing transitional housing'. ABC11 (Aug 2024) reported the state funding cut and that it might close, but I found no closure notice. The site's newest date is 2023.

name: El Vinculo Hispano
concern: offices only in Siler City and Sanford, not Chapel Hill; phone 919-742-1448 (listed 1488)

resolution.reason: The organization's site lists offices only in Siler City (404 N. Holly Ave, 919-742-1448) and Sanford (1225 N. Horner Blvd, 919-292-0177), and its programs center on Chatham County. Pittsboro is in Chatham County, so it serves a covered town. Both listed addresses and the phone number (1488) were wrong.

name: Haven House Outreach Center
concern: youth drop-in, not a shelter; (919) 833-3312 belongs to other Haven House programs

resolution.reason: Haven House's site lists no Outreach Center or drop-in center, and no shelter for ages 18+. It lists Street Outreach, Coordinated Entry intake for ages 18–24 (919-980-2015), Transition in Place, and Wrenn House (already a separate listing). 1008 Bullard Ct and 919-833-3312 are the main office.

name: Asylum Seekers Advocacy Project
concern: national online group; URL redirects to asaptogether.org

resolution.reason: asylumadvocacy.org now redirects (301) to asaptogether.org/en/. ASAP is a national online membership organization with no local office.

name: St. Thomas More
concern: own page says utility help only, not rent; listed URL 403s, ministry page at 5520.sites.ecatholic.com

resolution.reason: The parish's Financial Assistance Ministry page says it helps Chapel Hill/Carrboro residents with a utility disconnect notice once every 12 months, and 'We do not provide rental assistance.' The ministry line is 919-942-6216, Monday 8:30–11:30am. 919-942-1040 is the parish office. stmchapelhill.org returns 403. I read the ministry page through search results because a direct fetch also returned 403.

name: Good Samaritan Fund
concern: now covers utilities and food only; utility applications closed until Dec 1

resolution.reason: The fund's page now says it provides 'financial assistance for utilities and food'; housing and transportation are no longer mentioned. It also says 'Applications are closed, and will open again December 1.' Utility requests are taken by online application, not by phone or in person on first Mondays.

name: Wake Tech ESL
concern: interest form currently closed

resolution.reason: The flag was wrong. The official ESL page (checked Nov 10, 2026) shows an active 'ESL interest form' button and no closed notice; the 'closed' wording appears only in old search snippets. I replaced the named contact (Tyler Richie, 919-307-9304), which I couldn't find anywhere on Wake Tech's site, with the college's main number, and updated the enrollment steps.

name: CWS Immigrant Solidarity Fund
concern: URL redirects to cwsdurham.org/isf/; waitlist several months

resolution.reason: cwsrdu.org/immigrantsolidarityfund/ redirects to cwsdurham.org and the redirect target 404s. The current page is at cwsdurham.org/isf/. It says average waits are 'currently several months' and lists the Triangle group as covering Durham, Orange, and Wake.

name: El Pueblo Familias Seguras
concern: a free Spanish-only PDF planning guide, not a service

resolution.reason: The Familias Seguras page describes it as a guide 'designed to help immigrant families in North Carolina prepare for emergencies', available as English and Spanish PDFs. It is not a service. The listed URL pointed straight to the Spanish PDF with tracking parameters. I kept it as a free resource but relabeled it as a guide.
